translation_notes: cfg.sosa.Observation / cfg.sosa.dateTime -> sosa:Observation / sosa:dateTime, RDF.type -> a, RDFS.comment/label -> rdfs:comment/rdfs:label; the four obsgraph.add(...) calls merge into one g{ ... } island with a ; list

FINDING: obsgraph += g{...} is an augmented assignment, so unlike obsgraph.add(...) it makes obsgraph a function-local name; the translation needs an extra `global obsgraph` statement (the transpiled code raised UnboundLocalError without it). The idiomatic += form is NOT a drop-in replacement for .add() when the target graph is a module global - it only works out of the box when the graph is a parameter or a local (as in the BrickSchema reference example).

the @prefix declarations hard-code the sosa IRI at transpile time, where the original looked cfg.sosa up at run time; the `from PySOSA import config as cfg` import is kept on both sides (a @prefix produces no runtime Namespace) but cfg is no longer read on the ldpy side

context shim PySOSA/ (local package with __init__.py and config.py): config.py carries only the `#Ontology namespaces` block copied verbatim from the corpus checkout, so the region-s import line `from PySOSA import config as cfg` stays byte-identical on both sides

demo harness added IDENTICALLY at the end of original.py and translated.ldpy: the region is a constructor writing into the module-level obsgraph, so nothing would call it; two observations are built (distinct blank-node subjects, same label) and the driver compares module state by graph isomorphism
Literal(datetime) in the original literalises the datetime CLASS object (a latent bug in the source); it is kept as-is and interpolated unchanged
negative control run: renaming sosa:dateTime in the island makes the driver report equivalent=false
